<mxfile host="Electron"> <diagram name="System Architecture" id="0"> <mxGraphModel dx="-1014" dy="-585" grid="0" gridSize="10" guides="1" tooltips="1" connect="1" arrows="1" fold="0" page="0" pageScale="1" pageWidth="1980" pageHeight="2300" math="0" shadow="0"> <root> <mxCell id="0" /> <mxCell id="1" parent="0" /> <mxCell id="title" parent="1" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=24;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#333333;" value="Climbing Wall Force Dashboard — System Architecture
<font style="font-size:14px;font-weight:normal">Four 3‑axis load cells → PhidgetBridge boards → USB → Flask backend → React frontend. Raw voltage ratios travel the wire; calibration to Newtons happens in the browser.</font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="70" width="1900" x="40" y="20" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bandA" parent="1" style="swimlane;startSize=36;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;fillColor=none;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=16;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#a06800;align=left;spacingLeft=16;verticalAlign=middle;collapsible=0;container=1;pointerEvents=0;swimlaneFillColor=none;" value="1 · Climbing wall — physical sensors" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="230" width="1900" x="40" y="120" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="axisnote" parent="bandA" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=12;fontColor=#7a5a00;" value="<b>Sensor (board) frame — the canonical frame everywhere downstream:</b> X = along the wall (in‑plane) · Y = sideways (right) · Z = out of the wall. The wall‑decline angle θ is NEVER applied here." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="26" width="1760" x="80" y="46" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="lh" parent="bandA" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffe6cc;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=13;" value="<b>Left Hand hold</b>
3‑axis load cell (X, Y, Z)
<font style="font-size:11px">3 strain‑gauge bridges</font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="112" width="380" x="80" y="92" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="rh" parent="bandA" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffe6cc;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=13;" value="<b>Right Hand hold</b>
3‑axis load cell (X, Y, Z)
<font style="font-size:11px">3 strain‑gauge bridges</font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="112" width="380" x="540" y="92" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="lf" parent="bandA" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffe6cc;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=13;" value="<b>Left Foot hold</b>
3‑axis load cell (X, Y, Z)
<font style="font-size:11px">3 strain‑gauge bridges</font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="112" width="380" x="1000" y="92" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="rf" parent="bandA" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffe6cc;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=13;" value="<b>Right Foot hold</b>
3‑axis load cell (X, Y, Z)
<font style="font-size:11px">3 strain‑gauge bridges</font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="112" width="380" x="1460" y="92" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bandB" parent="1" style="swimlane;startSize=36;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;fillColor=none;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=16;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#a06800;align=left;spacingLeft=16;verticalAlign=middle;collapsible=0;container=1;pointerEvents=0;swimlaneFillColor=none;" value="2 · Hardware link — PhidgetBridge over USB" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="400" width="1900" x="40" y="410" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="brlh" parent="bandB" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffe6cc;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=12;" value="<b>PhidgetBridge</b>
S/N <b>293698</b> — wire group 1
channels 0,1,2 = X,Y,Z · gain 128" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="110" width="380" x="80" y="60" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="brrh" parent="bandB" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffe6cc;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=12;" value="<b>PhidgetBridge</b>
S/N <b>293701</b> — wire group 3
channels 0,1,2 = X,Y,Z · gain 128" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="110" width="380" x="540" y="60" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="brlf" parent="bandB" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffe6cc;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=12;" value="<b>PhidgetBridge</b>
S/N <b>481661</b> — wire group 0
channels 0,1,2 = X,Y,Z · gain 128" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="110" width="380" x="1000" y="60" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="brrf" parent="bandB" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffe6cc;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=12;" value="<b>PhidgetBridge</b>
S/N <b>481689</b> — wire group 2
channels 0,1,2 = X,Y,Z · gain 128" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="110" width="380" x="1460" y="60" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="hub" parent="bandB" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffe6cc;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=13;" value="<b>Powered USB hub</b>
4 bridges → one USB port on the host machine
<i>There is no Raspberry Pi and no Web Serial.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="80" width="380" x="760" y="260" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="hwnote" parent="bandB" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=12;fontColor=#7a5a00;" value="<b>Which physical board is which body part is configuration, not code:</b> the <i>index</i> of a serial in <b>bridgeSerials[]</b> (backend/phidget_config.json) is its wire group. If sensors look swapped in the GUI, reorder that list — never edit the parser." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="26" width="1760" x="80" y="356" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bandC" parent="1" style="swimlane;startSize=36;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;fillColor=none;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=16;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#4d7a35;align=left;spacingLeft=16;verticalAlign=middle;collapsible=0;container=1;pointerEvents=0;swimlaneFillColor=none;" value="3 · Backend — Python / Flask on the host machine (localhost:5001)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="300" width="1900" x="40" y="850" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="stream" parent="bandC" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=6;" value="<b>phidget_stream.py</b>

• opens 12 VoltageRatioInput channels, non‑blocking
 (backend runs fine with hardware unplugged)
• broadcast loop @ <b>100 Hz</b> (dataIntervalMs = 10)
• a detached channel is forced to 0.0, never frozen
• one bounded queue per WS client — a slow client
 drops its own samples, not everyone's" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="170" width="440" x="60" y="60" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="appy" parent="bandC" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=6;" value="<b>app.py — Flask REST API</b>

<b>POST /api/jump</b> — the only physics here: wall‑frame force → global vertical, minus body
weight, double‑integrated a→v→x. dt comes from phidget_config.json, never from the client.
<b>GET/POST /api/calibration</b> · <b>/api/calibration/profiles</b> — store & validate axisSigns / axisScales
<b>POST /api/recordings/save</b> · <b>GET /api/recordings[/<id>/data]</b> — write CSV + meta, list 5 newest, downsample to 1000 pts
<b>GET /api/phidgets/status</b> — per‑board attach state; also boots the channels on first call" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="170" width="560" x="620" y="60" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="disk" parent="bandC" style="shape=cylinder3;boundedLbl=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#666666;fontSize=12;fontColor=#333333;" value="<b>Host disk</b>
saved_recordings/*.csv + *.meta.json (sensor‑frame Newtons)
calibration_settings.json (written into the frontend src tree)
calibration_profiles.json (gitignored, local only)
phidget_config.json (serials, gain, sample interval)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="110" width="540" x="1300" y="60" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="cnote" parent="bandC" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=12;fontColor=#4d7a35;" value="<b>The backend does no calibration.</b> It serves raw voltage ratios (~1e‑6) and one physics endpoint. · Flask runs <b>use_reloader=False</b>: a forked second process would fight for the single‑open Phidget channels and both would fail to attach." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="35" width="1020" x="60" y="250" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bandD" parent="1" style="swimlane;startSize=36;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;fillColor=none;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;fontSize=16;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#3d5a80;align=left;spacingLeft=16;verticalAlign=middle;collapsible=0;container=1;pointerEvents=0;swimlaneFillColor=none;" value="4 · Frontend — React + Vite (localhost:5173, proxies /api → 5001)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="800" width="1900" x="40" y="1210" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="d1" parent="bandD" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=6;" value="<b>useBackendStream</b>

WebSocket client for /api/stream.
connect() resolves only once the socket
is truly open. Surfaces hardwareWarning
(partial attach) and mockModeActive
(backend unreachable → synthetic data)." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="140" width="360" x="60" y="70" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="d2" parent="bandD" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=6;" value="<b>sensor-dashboard.tsx</b>
handleSerialLine(line)

The only orchestrator. Wires the stream to
its three sinks through stable refs.
No business logic lives here." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="130" width="360" x="60" y="270" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="d3" parent="bandD" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=6;" value="<b>parseSerialLine</b> (utils/serialParser.ts)
<i>the transform pipeline — where raw becomes Newtons</i>

<b>1</b> parse 12 floats, reject any non‑finite line
<b>2</b> remap wire groups <b>[1, 3, 0, 2]</b> → GUI order
 [Left Hand, Right Hand, Left Foot, Right Foot] × (X,Y,Z)
<b>3</b> × axisSigns → <b>signedRaw</b> (pre‑tare, pre‑scale)
<b>4</b> − runtime tare (the volatile zero)
<b>5</b> × axisScales → <b>values</b> — Newtons, <b>sensor frame</b>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="250" width="440" x="480" y="70" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="d5" parent="bandD" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#e1d5e7;strokeColor=#9673a6;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=6;" value="<b>Calibration & tare state</b>

<b>useCalibration</b> — the wizard: capture averages per
axis, least‑squares fit → <b>axisScales</b> (persisted)
<b>useTareOffset</b> — "Zero Sensors": mean of the last
~150 samples → <b>runtime offset</b> (volatile, never saved
to the backend; only cached in localStorage)

Both consume <b>signedRaw</b>, so their results do not
depend on whichever calibration is active." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="190" width="440" x="480" y="390" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="d4" parent="bandD" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=6;" value="<b>useSensorData</b>

Live buffer in a <i>mutable ref</i> — no
re‑render per sample. Capped at
360 000 samples (~1 h @ 100 Hz).
Copies a display slice to React state
at 20 fps, decimated to ≤1000 points." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="180" width="360" x="1020" y="70" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="d11" parent="bandD" style="shape=cylinder3;boundedLbl=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#666666;fontSize=12;fontColor=#333333;" value="<b>IndexedDB</b>
climbing‑wall/recordings (v2)
survives a page reload" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="280" x="1060" y="320" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="d10" parent="bandD" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=6;" value="<b>wallGeometry.toDisplayFrameReadings</b>

The <b>only</b> place the wall‑decline angle θ is
applied — at render time, as an opt‑in view.
"sensor" returns the same reference; "world"
maps a rotated copy.
<i>Applying θ earlier double‑corrects jump height.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="180" width="360" x="1460" y="70" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="d9" parent="bandD" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=6;" value="<b>UI — tabs & charts (Chart.js)</b>

• Force Magnitudes — ‖F‖ per sensor
• Components — X / Y / Z per sensor
• Jump Test — mass, angle, run, result
• Recordings — list, view, A/B compare, CSV
• Toolbar — connect, record, calibrate,
 Zero Sensors, world‑frame lock" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="200" width="360" x="1460" y="320" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="d12" parent="bandD" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;fontSize=12;" value="<b>REST clients</b>
jumpApi · recordingApi · calibrationProfiles
<i>always POST sensor‑frame values</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="130" width="360" x="1460" y="590" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="dnote" parent="bandD" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=12;fontColor=#3d5a80;" value="<b>The one invariant:</b> everything is stored in the <b>sensor (board) frame</b> — the live buffer, IndexedDB and the backend CSV alike. Never rotate on ingestion. If you find yourself applying θ in serialParser.ts, useSensorData.ts, or before a POST, that is the bug, not the fix." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="40" width="1760" x="60" y="730" as="geometry" /> div.div:
Climbing Wall Force Dashboard — System Architecture
Four 3‑axis load cells → PhidgetBridge boards → USB → Flask backend → React frontend. Raw voltage ratios travel the wire; calibration to Newtons happens in the browser.

Powered USB hub
4 bridges → one USB port on the host machine
There is no Raspberry Pi and no Web Serial.

div.div: Which physical board is which body part is configuration, not code: the index of a serial in bridgeSerials[] (backend/phidget_config.json) is its wire group. If sensors look swapped in the GUI, reorder that list — never edit the parser.

div.div: 3 · Backend — Python / Flask on the host machine (localhost:5001)

div.div:
phidget_stream.py
• opens 12 VoltageRatioInput channels, non‑blocking
(backend runs fine with hardware unplugged)
• broadcast loop @ 100 Hz (dataIntervalMs = 10)
• a detached channel is forced to 0.0, never frozen
• one bounded queue per WS client — a slow client
drops its own samples, not everyone's

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.div:
app.py — Flask REST API
POST /api/jump — the only physics here: wall‑frame force → global vertical, minus body
weight, double‑integrated a→v→x. dt comes from phidget_config.json, never from the client.
GET/POST /api/calibration · /api/calibration/profiles — store & validate axisSigns / axisScales
POST /api/recordings/save · GET /api/recordings[//data] — write CSV + meta, list 5 newest, downsample to 1000 pts
GET /api/phidgets/status — per‑board attach state; also boots the channels on first call

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 538px; height: 1px; padding-top: 968px; margin-left: 1311px;

div.div:
Host disk
saved_recordings/*.csv + *.meta.json (sensor‑frame Newtons)
calibration_settings.json (written into the frontend src tree)
calibration_profiles.json (gitignored, local only)
phidget_config.json (serials, gain, sample interval)

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1108px; margin-left: 72px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #4d7a35;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#4d7a35, #769d61); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: The backend does no calibration. It serves raw voltage ratios (~1e‑6) and one physics endpoint. · Flask runs use_reloader=False: a forked second process would fight for the single‑open Phidget channels and both would fail to attach.

div.div:
useBackendStream
WebSocket client for /api/stream.
connect() resolves only once the socket
is truly open. Surfaces hardwareWarning
(partial attach) and mockModeActive
(backend unreachable → synthetic data).

div.div:
sensor-dashboard.tsx
handleSerialLine(line)
The only orchestrator. Wires the stream to
its three sinks through stable refs.
No business logic lives here.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 426px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1283px; margin-left: 504px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
parseSerialLine (utils/serialParser.ts)
the transform pipeline — where raw becomes Newtons
1 parse 12 floats, reject any non‑finite line
2 remap wire groups [1, 3, 0, 2] → GUI order
[Left Hand, Right Hand, Left Foot, Right Foot] × (X,Y,Z)
3 × axisSigns → signedRaw (pre‑tare, pre‑scale)
4 − runtime tare (the volatile zero)
5 × axisScales → values — Newtons, sensor frame

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 426px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1603px; margin-left: 504px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Calibration & tare state
useCalibration — the wizard: capture averages per
axis, least‑squares fit → axisScales (persisted)
useTareOffset — "Zero Sensors": mean of the last
~150 samples → runtime offset (volatile, never saved
to the backend; only cached in localStorage)
Both consume signedRaw, so their results do not
depend on whichever calibration is active.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 346px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1283px; margin-left: 1044px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
useSensorData
Live buffer in a mutable ref — no
re‑render per sample. Capped at
360 000 samples (~1 h @ 100 Hz).
Copies a display slice to React state
at 20 fps, decimated to ≤1000 points.

div.div:
wallGeometry.toDisplayFrameReadings
The only place the wall‑decline angle θ is
applied — at render time, as an opt‑in view.
"sensor" returns the same reference; "world"
maps a rotated copy.
Applying θ earlier double‑corrects jump height.

div.div: The one invariant: everything is stored in the sensor (board) frame — the live buffer, IndexedDB and the backend CSV alike. Never rotate on ingestion. If you find yourself applying θ in serialParser.ts, useSensorData.ts, or before a POST, that is the bug, not the fix.

div.div:
Reading this diagram: follow the thick arrows top‑to‑bottom — that is one force sample's journey. The thick green arrow on the right is the only path back to the backend.
Two numbers to remember: 100 Hz (sample rate, set by dataIntervalMs) and 12 channels (4 boards × 3 axes, flat index = board×3 + axis).
Where things get calibrated: the wire carries raw voltage ratios; Newtons only exist after step 5 of parseSerialLine, in the browser.
